report:
### Conclusion
The claim that taking ibuprofen for COVID-19 worsens the infection is **false**. Comprehensive scientific studies and reviews by global health authorities show no evidence that ibuprofen or other nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) worsen COVID-19 severity or lead to poorer clinical outcomes.

### Evidence and Analysis
* **Origin of the Claim:** Early in the pandemic (March 2020), concerns emerged following anecdotal reports from French health officials and theoretical hypotheses suggesting NSAIDs might upregulate ACE2 receptors or mask infection symptoms.
* **Regulatory Guidance:** Leading health agencies, including the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) and the World Health Organization (WHO), evaluated the scientific evidence and clarified that taking ibuprofen does not worsen COVID-19 symptoms or increase infection risks.
* **Clinical Data:** Observational studies and systematic reviews comparing patients who used ibuprofen with those who did not found no significant link between ibuprofen use and adverse outcomes, such as higher mortality, ICU admission, or severe acute respiratory syndrome.

### Sources
* FDA Statement on NSAIDs and COVID-19: https://www.fda.gov/drugs/drug-alerts-and-statements/fda-advises-patients-use-non-steroidal-anti-inflammatory-drugs-nsaids-covid-19
* Study on Prescribed Ibuprofen and Severe COVID-19: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7537121/
* The Lancet Rheumatology Article: https://www.thelancet.com/journals/lanrhe/article/PIIS2665-9913(21)00144-2/fulltext
* WHO Clarification Report: https://www.cbc.ca/news/health/ibuprofen-covid-19-novel-coronavirus-1.5501496
